# eLearning 9.11. - 13.11. {-#elearning_9_11}

## 1. Review the material {-}

Go through everything we have covered together. Read the script at your own pace and revisit the
[animations](https://jdegenfellner.github.io/Script_QM1_ZHAW/animations/) we showed in class.
You are welcome to extend the animations with further elements that you find useful (using coding tools).

## 2. Standard deviations that are too large {-}

In class we noticed that Table 1 of a paper often reports a standard deviation that is too large for the scale of a
(semi-)continuous variable. Create realistic examples with scales you know and reproduce this phenomenon.

- What do the raw data look like in such cases?
- What goes wrong?

Please work on the following exercises of the chapter on [probability](#probs):

- [Exercise 2](#exercise2) (Bayes-teaser)

  Publications with data and code would be ideal, although they are probably rare.
  We need a few days of lead time so that everybody can look at the papers beforehand.
  I would not be surprised if we find errors.
- [Exercise 4](#exercise4) (Independent and disjoint)
